recovery.title: Recovery Phrase
recovery.warning: Write this down. It will NOT be shown again.

recovery.whyBody: This 24-word phrase is the ONLY way to recover your vault if every device fails. There is no server, no email reset, no phone number to call. If you lose the phrase and all your devices, your vault is gone forever.
recovery.example1: You buy a new laptop and your old one is already gone.
recovery.example2: Your phone is lost or destroyed and your laptop died last month.
recovery.example3: A house fire, flood, or theft takes every device at once.
recovery.example4: You return to Baluard after years away and need to set up a new device.
recovery.writeItDown: Write it on paper. Store it somewhere safe (safe, safety deposit box, fireproof bag). Screenshots and password managers are NOT safe enough — they can fail too.

recovery.sheetWarning: Anyone who can read these 24 words can open this vault. Store this file somewhere safe.

gitWhat.title: What is git, in plain words?
gitWhat.p1: Baluard keeps your vault in a git repository. Git is a time-tested tool (born in 2005, running millions of projects) whose whole job is keeping copies of your files in sync across devices and remembering every change.
gitWhat.p2: Think of the version history in Google Docs, or save points in a video game: every change gets its own entry, nothing is ever silently overwritten, and any device can catch up with the latest version at any time.
gitWhat.p3: The copies live in an account that you own, like GitHub, GitLab, or Codeberg. Baluard encrypts everything on your device first, so your account only ever stores scrambled data that only you can open.
gitWhat.p4: There is no Baluard server. Your vault never passes through computers we run.
